newsitem.title: UK: Jury retires in British soccer match-fixing trial.
newsitem.headline: Jury retires in British soccer match-fixing trial.

text.p: The jury in one of British soccer's most sensational match fixing trials retired on Friday to consider its verdict.

The prosecution alleges that former top players Bruce Grobbelaar, 39, John Fashanu, 34, Hans Segers, 35, and Malaysian businessman Heng Suan Lim, 32, conspired to give or accept corrupt payments to influence the result of matches.
It is alleged they were part of a plot involving an Asian betting syndicate to rig English premier league games.
The four men deny the allegations.
Lim, former Aston Villa and Wimbledon striker Fashanu and former Wimbledon keeper Segers are accused of conspiring to rig matches between 1991 and 1994.
Separately, Lim, Fashanu and former Liverpool and Southampton goalkeeper Grobbelaar are accused of a similar conspiracy between November 1992 and November 1994.
Grobbelaar also denies accepting 2,000 pounds ($3,270) from his former business partner Christopher Vincent for fixing or trying to fix games.

The jury of five men and six women retired on the 41st day of the trial. The jury at an earlier trial in the same case, which ended earlier this year, failed to reach a verdict. ($ = 0.610 British Pounds)
